title: Strict KEX: non-KEX message tolerated during the initial key exchange
quote: When strict KEX is enabled, implementations MUST terminate the connection if they receive a non-KEX message during the initial key exchange. / Unexpected packets for the purpose of strict KEX include messages that are otherwise valid at any time during the connection such as SSH2_MSG_DEBUG and SSH2_MSG_IGNORE.
rationale: After the client KEXINIT (strict KEX is then active, since the mapper offers it and the targets answer with kex-strict-s) and before the client NEWKEYS, any of IGNORE, DEBUG, UNIMPLEMENTED, SR_*, UA_* or CH_OPEN must be answered by DISCONNECT and/or connection close; any other output (NO_RESP, UNIMPLEMENTED, SERVICE_ACCEPT, ...) is a violation. This is the Terrapin countermeasure.
